title: KV lease-renewal contention causing intermittent tokens/sec collapse across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Lena Brooks
description: Summary: Multiple customers (notably FinSight and two hosted tenants) reported sudden drops in tokens/sec and TTFT spikes during sustained bursty workloads. Investigation shows worker threads entering prolonged waits on a KV lease-renewal lock under specific concurrency patterns (many short-lived sessions with repeated lease refreshes after warmstart). Impact: tokens/sec collapsed from ~9k to ~1.2k at peak for affected pools; 95p TTFT regressed from ~35ms to ~450ms for small prompt workloads. Affected environments: Hosted API region-us-west, Dedicated pools with mixed-model fanout, and Private VPC deployments that use our on-hosted KV sharding layer. This ticket tracks the engineering fix, rollout, and post-mortem artifacts.
root_cause_summary: Under high session churn (many short-lived requests using warmstart), the centralized KV lease manager experienced a renewal storm: concurrent renewals serialized on an exclusive mutex while also triggering background persistence/upsert paths. Serialization caused worker stalls and backpressure into the multiplex queue, collapsing tokens/sec and increasing TTFT. The pattern is amplified on Dedicated pools running heterogenous model fanout because each variant attempts renewals concurrently.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy a small cluster that uses the standard KV sharding configuration.
2) Run a synthetic workload with 200 short sessions/s, each performing a warmstart and sending 1-3 token-generation requests with random small contexts.
3) Observe KV lease-renewal RPC spikes in kube-proxy logs and worker thread stacks showing mutex wait on LeaseManager::renew().
4) Verify tokens/sec drop and TTFT spike with local load generator and metrics dashboard (token-rate and first-byte latency).
mitigations: Deploy temporary feature-flagged backoff: stagger lease-renewals with jitter and exponential backoff to prevent simultaneous renewals
Add in-process lease cache on worker to coalesce renewals across concurrent sessions (soft local cache with 5s TTL)
Introduce a circuit-breaker around the lease path so long-running renewals return degraded-but-serviceable response to avoid full worker stall
Rate-limit renewal persistence to the backing KV (20 ops/s per shard) as emergency throttle
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix, feature-flagged): push a minimal backoff + jitter on renew paths and enable in-host renewal coalescing behind FF. Phase 2: implement async renewal worker with pointer-stamp to avoid holding the mutex during network persistence. Phase 3: telemetry and tuning (per-shard renewal pacing) + opt-in global rollout for Dedicated pools. Each phase includes canary with metric gates (tokens/sec >= 80% baseline, 95p TTFT <= 2x baseline) before wider rollout.
rollback_plan: Revert feature flag and hotfix commit; revert traffic-split routing to reserve capacity to alternate pools; if revert is insufficient, scale Dedicated pool capacity for affected customers as temporary mitigation and open immediate incident (separate runbook).
monitoring_and_gates: Dashboards: tokens/sec, multiplex-queue-latency, lease-renewal-rps, lease-renewal-latency, worker-mutex-waits. Gates for canary: tokens/sec degradation < 10% from baseline and 95p TTFT < 1.5x baseline. Alerting: new high-severity alert on sustained lease-renewal mutex wait > 200ms across >5% workers.
customer_notes: FinSight escalation: ticket FS-2026-77; provided transient workaround to throttle client-side warmstart frequency. Customer accepted canary on their Dedicated pool for phased rollout. Legal/CS informed; CS will send proactive status updates every 4 hours until mitigated.
